title: Adoption Signal Prioritization Sprintboard
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sprintboard for the Customer Success team to prioritize adoption signals used in health scoring, identify fast experiments for QBR readiness, and lock down thresholds for renewal risk flags. It's intentionally rough — meant to capture hypotheses, quick QA checks, and a simple cadence for weight tuning before the March QBR cycle.

Scope and constraints:
- Focus on signals derived from platform behavior (usage, model calls, latency), adoption milestones (routes enabled, integrations), and qualitative touchpoints (NPS, support volume).
- We are NOT including deep financial signals (ARR deltas) here — that lives in Finance trackers but will be joined for final risk model.
- Prioritize signals that can be computed from existing event streams and the analytics warehouse within 48 hours.

Quick scoreboard (experiment buckets):
- Bucket A (measure now, high reliability): feature-usage-rate, weekly-active-seat-count, median-API-latency, failed-request-rate
- Bucket B (measure within 2 sprints): first-successful-deployment, KV-cache-hit-rate, prefix-cache-share
- Bucket C (exploratory): qualitative-adoption-index (SE notes + NPS tags), prompt-complexity-trends

Signal catalog (sample rows) — compute doc for each signal should include SQL and freshness window:
- feature-usage-rate: description=percent of customer users invoking Redwood API at least once per 7d; type=ratio; normalization=min-max across customer cohort; target correlation with renewal=positive; initial weight=0.18
- weekly-active-seat-count: description=distinct seats with >=1 token generated in 7d; type=count; normalization=log(1+x); initial weight=0.12
- median-api-latency: description=median server-side response latency p50 in ms; type=latency; normalization=inverse z-score (lower is better); initial weight=0.10
- failed-request-rate: description=client-visible errors / total requests 7d; type=ratio; normalization=inverse min-max; initial weight=0.14
- KV-cache-hit-rate: description=cache hits / cache lookups; type=ratio; normalization=min-max; initial weight=0.09
- demo-or-internal-usage-flag: description=binary flag to exclude trial/demo accounts; type=binary; normalization=exclude if true; initial weight=0.00 (filter)

Scoring formula (working):
- Normalize each raw signal to a 0..1 scale (choose min-max or robust min-max with 1st/99th percentiles).
- Weighted sum: HEALTH_SCORE = sum_i (w_i * normalized_signal_i)
- Regularization: during weight tuning apply L1 penalty to prefer sparse signals (helps interpretability).
- Score range: 0 — 1 ; higher = healthier.

Initial risk buckets (provisional cutoffs):
- GREEN: HEALTH_SCORE >= 0.65 — low-touch QBR cadence (6–12 months), automated renewal nudges
- YELLOW: 0.40 <= HEALTH_SCORE < 0.65 — proactive outreach, enable adoption playbooks, run targeted experiments
- RED: HEALTH_SCORE < 0.40 — immediate AE/CSM engagement, technical enablement, potential renewal risk

Risk flag overrides and rule exceptions:
- If failed-request-rate > 5% or median-api-latency > 1500ms, force a RED flag regardless of score (operational reliability override).
- New accounts (< 30 days) should be evaluated by time-normalized signals (use day-weighted lookback) to avoid false-reds.
- Manual override capability for CSMs with required justification note stored in the account timeline (audit).

Weight tuning plan (two-week sprint):
1) Week 1: backtest weights on last 12 months of renewal outcomes. Use logistic regression (weights constrained 0..0.3) and a holdout 20% sample for calibration.
2) Week 2: A/B test two scoring variants in QBR prep bucket (Variant A = production weights, Variant B = regressed weights). Compare precision/recall for churn signals and number of manual overrides triggered.
3) Deliverable: recommended weights + a one-page rationalization for GTM and Finance sign-off.

Operational checks / data QA checklist before QBR ingestion:
- Verify event schema drift (tokens, model_id, customer_id) in the past 60 days.
- Confirm identity mapping between analytics customer_id and billing account_id (join coverage >= 98%).
- Confirm missing-value handling: replace nulls with cohort median for non-critical signals.
- Establish audit query to list accounts with manual overrides in the last 180 days.

QBR slides & data pulls (minimum):
- Slide 1: Health-score distribution histogram + median by ARR bucket
- Slide 2: Top 10 customers moved from GREEN->YELLOW->RED in last quarter (with root cause tags: product, usage, ops)
- Slide 3: Model performance: Precision@K for churn alerts (K=25) and number of false positives by CSM feedback
- Slide 4: Actionable plays recommended for YELLOW cohort for next 90 days

Play examples (short):
- Low-usage nudge: Automated sequence (email + in-app guide + 1-touch from CSM) triggered when feature-usage-rate drops > 30% QoQ and score in YELLOW.
- Reliability escalation: If operational override triggers RED, triage with SRE + technical CSM within 24 hours; create incident-tagged case and track time-to-resolution.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Normalize by customer size vs seat count? (action: test both and report lift in model AUC)
- Include negative-sentiment support tickets as a weighted signal or a binary override? (action: Priya to fetch last 300 support threads and run simple sentiment tagger)
- How to treat customers with multiple deployments across regions — per-customer aggregate or per-deployment rows? (action: Marcus to prototype per-deployment scoring, see tradeoffs)

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Marcus: run initial backtest and post results to linked confluence page (ETA: 2026-02-10)
notes: Working doc: capture of brainstorm and sprint tasks for health scoring. Noters: Elena. Use this as single source of truth for the March QBR signal freeze. Update status to in_review when weights are proposed.
